title: The ink on the pocket
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: A pen uncapped in the pocket. The stain on the canvas, spreading, over a panel. Wood feels it and doesn't take the pen out. Let it. The pocket has ink now. It's where the pens go; it should say so.

panels.composition: The classroom. WOOD at the back in the coat, the pad, a pen going into the pocket uncapped without his noticing.

image.prompt: a young man at the back of a classroom slipping an uncapped pen into his canvas coat's pocket without noticing, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The pocket. A dark spot on the canvas. Spreading.

image.prompt: close on a dark ink stain spreading on a canvas coat pocket, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood's hand going to the pocket. Feeling it. Not taking the pen out.

image.prompt: close on a young man's hand pressing on an ink-stained coat pocket and leaving the pen inside, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The INSTRUCTOR at the board. Wood, the coat, the stain. The strip forty strokes now. The coat has its three things: cuff, button, ink. It's the coat. Done.

image.prompt: a young man in a stained chore coat at the back of a classroom while an instructor writes on the board, drawn in forty sparse strokes, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen over rough blue pencil; xerox grain; stark spotting; rain in frantic vertical hatching (Arc 1's aesthetic)

notes: Cuff, button, ink. The coat's done. Forty strokes.
